subject: Marketplace invoice entity split — reconciliation request and payout hold
messages:
From: Acme Corp Billing <billing@acme.example>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-08-02T14:08:00-07:00
Subject: AWS Marketplace invoices — entity attribution causing payout hold

Hi Jordan,

We're seeing two charges on our AWS Marketplace statement for the July usage window that were attributed to the platform (Redwood) rather than to our seller entity. Because of that split, AWS is holding the related payout for our account until we provide evidence that those lines should be remitted to Acme.

Attached: acme_invoice_20280801.pdf (redacted invoice), summary table in CSV available on request.

Can you confirm what evidence Redwood can provide (e.g., marketplace metering IDs, listing IDs, seller-account mapping) so AWS will release the hold? We are past the normal payout cutoff and this is blocking funds we need to settle downstream.

Thanks,
Lauren Reed
Billing Ops
Acme Corp

[attachment: acme_invoice_20280801.pdf]

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Reed <lauren.reed@acme.example>, Acme Corp Billing <billing@acme.example>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-08-02T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace invoices — entity attribution causing payout hold

Hi Lauren — thanks for the heads up and sorry for the disruption.

Quick plan:
- Marcus (finance) will advise on the credit-memo / payout fix.
- Hannah (marketplace ops) will open / escalate an AWS case to request immediate release and provide the metering evidence.

To move fast, can you send: the AWS invoice line numbers, the AWS usage record IDs (if available), and the Seller ID you expect to be credited? If you prefer, you can drop the CSV you mentioned and we'll extract the lines.

We understand the timing sensitivity — I'll push this as high priority. Estimated next update by EOD tomorrow unless we get AWS confirmation sooner.

Jordan Blake
Senior Account Exec, Marketplaces
Redwood Inference

[internal note: volley to marketplace ops & finance — need packing list for credit memo]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Reed <lauren.reed@acme.example>
Date: 2028-08-03T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace invoices — entity attribution causing payout hold

Thanks Jordan / Lauren. Quick accounting perspective:

- If the usage lines were invoiced under Redwood's marketplace seller listing by mistake, we can issue a credit memo and re-invoice under the Acme seller ID. That flow requires AWS marketplace support to accept the evidence bundle and allow a payout reallocation.
- For the credit memo we'll need: original invoice number, exact line amounts, GL codes to map the reversal, and confirmation of the recipient legal entity (Acme legal name + tax id).

Hannah: please confirm what evidence (metering records / listing ID) we can supply directly from Redwood's side. Lauren, if you can attach the CSV with the usage record IDs I can draft the credit memo and the journal entries.

Marcus Lin
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

[signature includes accounting phone; internal priority: high]

Date: 2028-08-04T07:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace invoices — entity attribution causing payout hold

Jordan / Marcus / Hannah — attaching the CSV extract you asked for: acme_ledger_aug.csv. It has the AWS usage-id column and the invoice line numbers.

A couple clarifications:
- The seller ID that should receive the payout is: 9-ACME-SELLER-01
- The affected invoice on our side is INV-ACME-2028-07-21 (attached PDF for convenience).

We're available for a quick 20-minute call if it speeds up the case with AWS; otherwise, please escalate and let us know what exact packet to upload to AWS.

Thanks — Lauren
Billing Ops
Acme Corp

Date: 2028-08-14T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace invoices — entity attribution causing payout hold

Hi all — quick summary and next steps (action owners in parentheses):

1) Evidence bundle: Lauren sent acme_ledger_aug.csv with usage record IDs and invoice references (Lauren).
2) Redwood evidence we can provide: listing ID (redwood-listing-101), internal metering export with usage-records and timestamps (Hannah). I've attached a draft credit memo for Marcus to review (redwood_credit_memo_draft.pdf).
3) Proposed remediation path:
   - Hannah will open an AWS Marketplace case (CASE-# pending) with the evidence bundle and request allocation of the disputed lines to seller 9-ACME-SELLER-01. (Hannah)
   - Marcus will prepare the credit memo and journal entries to enable Redwood to reverse the platform-side recognition if AWS accepts the reallocation. (Marcus)
   - Jordan will coordinate with Acme on any short-form attestation AWS requires and will request a 72-hour expedited review given payout timing. (Jordan)

Hannah — can you confirm ETA to open the AWS case and whether we need any additional signed attestation from Acme? Marcus — please confirm if the attached draft credit memo looks sufficient from your side.

Lauren — our ask from Acme: please provide the legal entity tax ID for re-invoicing, and confirm whether you want the credit memo issued to your AP or applied as a contra to the next payout. Either is fine but we need the preference for documentation.

Links: HubSpot deal (https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/67890) and the evidence Drive folder (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c4d-acme-billing-evidence).

I will follow up with the AWS case number once Hannah opens it. Target: get payout released within 7 business days if AWS accepts the reallocation; otherwise we will coordinate a credit memo + reissuance and updates to the next remittance cycle.

Thanks team — moving to high priority.

Jordan Blake
Senior Account Exec, Marketplaces
Redwood Inference
